correctness.rationale: Detailed balance reconstructs all stationary count weights; exchangeability gives pair moment identities. A tilted-Gamma iid-Bernoulli mixture proves strict pair covariance positivity for all finite n and v>0. n=2 gives a strictly increasing elementary rational Pearson correlation. n=3 gives a rational correlation whose parameter derivative numerator is a quartic with exactly one sign variation and opposite endpoint signs, proving exactly one positive simple zero and a strict global maximum for every u>0; p3 has a positive derivative. For n>=3, weight ratios yield zero high-colonization correlation and continuity forces an interior peak. Exact symbolic and 1,200 rational independent balance/correlation checks passed; they corroborate rather than replace the full proof.

originality.rationale: The original 2002 source provides the birth–death stationary distribution and moments and is credited. The distinct new structural theorem is a parameter-uniform unique Pearson-correlation maximum for three patches, strict two-patch monotonicity and the sharp n>=3 reentrant-onset distinction. Closely relevant literature on contact-process monotonicity and positive covariance lacks that explicit conclusion in accessible material. Uniform Descartes sign structure and asymptotic patch-number analysis are not a table lookup; unresolved complete-text comparisons leave an acknowledged historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: General stationary distribution and higher moments of the exact same model were published in 2002, so formula-level originality cannot be claimed; the assessed novelty is the sharp qualitative correlation-response theorem.
Full technical articles on complete-graph SIS covariance (2012 and 2015) and SIS positivity (2014) could not be read; a historical-priority result may be present there.
Semantic literature searches and existing research records do not certify worldwide uniqueness; independent historical-priority review remains necessary.

value.rationale: Stationary pairwise Pearson correlation quantifies cross-patch occupancy synchronization beyond the marginal occupancy rate. The theorem identifies a sharp minimum habitat count for a nonmonotone response to internal connectivity, supplies a unique connectivity maximizing correlation for every positive immigration parameter at n=3, and shows marginal occupancy rises despite the peak. This universal finite-population structural distinction is mathematically motivated and not an arbitrary example; it can benchmark exact stochastic metapopulation models while remaining explicitly idealized.
